goal:
A reviewer asked me to double-check a value from the 2025 paper by Ferreira and colleagues on graph sparsification in Journal of Alpine Hydrology (http://review.example/pdf/fada1b8e609b1d5adbc579642bbf1c.pdf).
It has to be the WWWX 2025 camera-ready version. What estimated capacity does Table 2 report for station L-08? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: A Stochastic Model of Graph Sparsification

paragraphs: We study graph sparsification across five monitoring stations using a nonparametric model.
Authors: Oskar Ferreira, Chiara Navarro. Published in Journal of Alpine Hydrology, 2025.
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report estimated capacity measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional estimated capacity at 1.7 bits/param; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of graph sparsification relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station S-12.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Quiroga et al. (2019). [2] Ilunga and Wenzel (2021). [3] Vasquez et al. (2022).
